evidence.Workflow / Use Case: Building sovereign supercomputing capacity for general and sector-specific large language models
evidence.Claim / Evidence Summary: Brazil announced about 2.3 billion reais of AI investments split across U.S.- and China-linked projects, including 1.3 billion reais for a Huawei/iFlytek supercomputing project and 1 billion reais for a separate top-10-class AI supercomputer tender.
evidence.Time Horizon / Target Date: Supercomputer expected operational by end-2027; China cooperation scheduled to start July 2027
evidence.Named AI Vendor / Model: Huawei / iFlytek; Nvidia expected for separate tender
evidence.Likely Value Capturer: Brazilian AI ecosystem; infrastructure and chip suppliers
evidence.Constraint / Bottleneck: Tender execution; construction; power; supplier diversification; geopolitical balancing
evidence.Source Type: Government announcement via independent news report
evidence.Source Title: Brazil launches AI supercomputer push, splits projects between Chinese, US firms
evidence.Supporting Excerpt (≤20 words): investments of about 2.3 billion reais ($444.2 million) to bolster its artificial intelligence ecosystem
evidence.Notes: Missed late-Aug. 20 publication recovered during the Aug. 21 Latin America rotation. Records announced funding and planned capacity, not an operating deployment. Nvidia is expected by officials to win the separate tender but had not been awarded it at collection time.
